Container.Name: tldw-redis
Container.Overview: Redis for tl;dw (Too Long, Didn't Watch) - the job queue and cache the tl;dw API server runs its background work through. TWO CONTAINERS, STARTED IN ORDER: tldw-redis first, then tldw-server. There is no template equivalent of compose depends_on, so nothing enforces that for you; tldw-server expects Redis to be reachable at its REDIS_URL when it starts, and you build that URL from this machine's address and the host port below. GIVE TL;DW ITS OWN: this container runs with a 512 MB memory ceiling and an allkeys-lru eviction policy, exactly as upstream's single-user compose file does, which means that under memory pressure it throws away the least recently used keys - acceptable for a cache and for this queue at upstream's sizing, destructive for anything else that might be sharing a Redis with it. STORAGE: the /data mount holds the append-only file, so the queue survives a restart. Losing it does not lose your ingested corpus - that lives on the tl;dw API container's own mount - it loses whatever work was queued. EXPOSURE: this publishes Redis on every interface of this machine with no password, because that is how the API container reaches it on the stock bridge network; keep it on a network you trust. IMAGE TAG: redis:7-alpine is a rolling tag, so unlike its sibling this container can take an upstream version change on an Update - see the comment at the top of the template file. The Redis command line is set in Post Arguments rather than as variables, because that is how this image is configured.
Container.Description: Redis for tl;dw - job queue and cache. Start this before tldw-server. Dedicated instance: it evicts under memory pressure.

Config.Name: Redis Port
Config.Description: Host port Redis is published on. The container always listens on 6379 internally - change the host side only. The default here is deliberately not 6379, so that installing this does not collide with a Redis you already run. Whatever you pick, it goes into tldw-server's REDIS_URL as redis://<server-ip>:<this-port>/0. ⚠️ This publishes Redis on your network with NO PASSWORD: anyone who can reach the port can read and write the queue. There is no field here to set one, because the API container has to reach it and this template does not carry that credential - so keep it on a trusted network.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Where the append-only file lives, which is what makes the queue survive a restart. Set an absolute path on a POOL (e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/tldw-redis/data). Without it the queue is written into the container layer and lost on the next update - which loses queued and in-flight jobs, though not the ingested corpus itself. Unlike the API container's mount, this one does not care who owns the directory: the official Redis image sets the ownership itself before dropping privileges.
